title: Terms from founder life, briefly explained.
intro: A focused glossary for terms you encounter while building a startup and working as a founder.
professionalNote: For legal or tax questions, the Library is not a substitute for individual professional advice.
setupPrompt: Relevant to your team right now?

updates.title: What founders should know
updates.intro: A curated selection of legal and regulatory developments that may be relevant to startups, briefly contextualized and linked directly to the official source.
updates.disclaimer: CoFoundery presents a selection of relevant developments and does not claim to be complete. These notes are not a substitute for individual legal review.

ki_mig_2026.title: New German rules implementing the EU AI Act
ki_mig_2026.relevance: This may be relevant if your startup develops, provides, or uses AI systems. The KI-MIG governs the German implementation of the EU AI Act and designates the responsible market surveillance authorities, among other matters.

dadg_2026.title: German implementation of the EU Data Act
dadg_2026.relevance: This may be relevant to startups whose products or services are affected by the EU Data Act rules on access to and use of data. The DADG governs implementation in Germany and designates the competent authority.

electronic_withdrawal_function_2026.title: Electronic withdrawal function for online contracts
electronic_withdrawal_function_2026.relevance: Relevant to businesses that conclude certain distance contracts with consumers through an online interface. Section 356a of the German Civil Code provides for an electronic withdrawal function in this context.

termPage.setupTitle: Comes up in these setup topics

bootstrapping.shortDefinition: Building a company primarily with the founders’ own resources and operating revenue rather than external equity financing.

burn_rate.shortDefinition: The amount of cash a company uses on a net basis over a given period, often measured monthly.

cap_table.shortDefinition: A record of who owns which shares or other equity interests in a company.

deadlock.shortDefinition: A decision-making stalemate in which the agreed voting rules or responsibilities cannot produce an outcome.

dilution.shortDefinition: The reduction in an existing stakeholder’s percentage ownership when new shares are issued.

drag_along_tag_along.shortDefinition: Contractual rules for the sale of company shares: drag-along can require certain shareholders to join a sale under defined conditions; tag-along can give other shareholders the right to participate in another shareholder’s sale on comparable terms.

esop_vsop.shortDefinition: Employee participation models: An ESOP typically uses actual shares or options for actual shares. A VSOP contractually mirrors an equity interest without directly creating shareholder status.

founder_agreement.shortDefinition: An agreement between founders that records central rules about their collaboration, ownership, and possible changes.

founder_exit.shortDefinition: A founder leaving the operating team, the company’s ownership structure, or both, with possible consequences for roles and equity.

good_bad_leaver.shortDefinition: Contractual categories for different ways of leaving a company that may carry different consequences for equity rights.

ip_assignment.shortDefinition: Contractual arrangements through which intellectual property rights or corresponding rights of use – such as rights in code, designs, trademarks, or inventions – are assigned to a company.

mvp.shortDefinition: A Minimum Viable Product is a deliberately limited first product version used to test core assumptions with real users.

pivot.shortDefinition: A fundamental change in product, business model, or target market based on new evidence.

pre_money_post_money.shortDefinition: Pre-money is a company’s valuation before a financing round; post-money includes the newly invested capital.

product_market_fit.shortDefinition: The point at which a product meets a meaningful market need well enough for sustained demand to become evident.

reverse_vesting.shortDefinition: An arrangement where shares have already been transferred but may remain subject to repurchase or retransfer rights that reduce over time.

runway.shortDefinition: The estimated time a company can continue operating with its available cash at its current rate of spending.

term_sheet.shortDefinition: A summary of the main proposed terms of an investment or financing before the detailed agreements are drafted.

vesting.shortDefinition: A mechanism that defines the period over which equity rights are gradually treated as earned or non-forfeitable and what consequences an early departure may have.

convertible_loan.shortDefinition: A loan whose repayment claim is converted, or can be converted, into equity under agreed conditions.

cliff.shortDefinition: The lock-in period at the start of a vesting plan: leave before it ends and you keep nothing. Twelve months is common.

slicing_pie.shortDefinition: A model that does not fix shares upfront but keeps recalculating them from what each person actually contributed — time, money, materials.

liquidation_preference.shortDefinition: The promise to investors that they get their money back first when the company is sold, before the rest is distributed.

company_valuation.shortDefinition: The value founders and investors agree on for a funding round. It is negotiated, not measured.

funding_rounds.shortDefinition: The usual sequence from pre-seed through seed to Series A and beyond. Each step stands for a stage of maturity and an order of magnitude, not a fixed amount.

business_angel.shortDefinition: A private individual who invests their own money in young companies and usually brings experience and contacts along.

due_diligence.shortDefinition: The examination of a company before an investment: numbers, contracts, rights, risks. Whatever is messy here costs negotiating room later.

exist_grant.shortDefinition: A German public grant that covers a year of living costs for founders coming out of universities so they can work on their idea.

hidden_profit_distribution.shortDefinition: When the company gives a shareholder more than would be usual between strangers — an inflated salary, say. The tax office retroactively treats it as a distribution of profit.

gbr.shortDefinition: The simplest shared legal form: it comes into being as soon as several people pursue a common purpose together. Everyone is liable with their private assets.

ug.shortDefinition: A variant of the GmbH that can be founded with one euro of share capital. In exchange, part of the profit must be retained until 25,000 euros are reached.

gmbh.shortDefinition: The most common legal form for startups in Germany. Liability is limited to company assets; founding it requires 25,000 euros of share capital and a notary appointment.

share_capital.shortDefinition: The money or assets the shareholders put into the company at the start. Afterwards it belongs to the company, not to the individuals.

contribution_in_kind.shortDefinition: A contribution that is not money but, for example, equipment, software or rights. Its value has to be substantiated.

commercial_register.shortDefinition: The public directory listing companies with their seat, management and powers of representation. Anyone can look inside.

notarization.shortDefinition: Some steps only take effect once a notary records them — founding a GmbH, or transferring shares. Without it the agreement is void.

personal_guarantee.shortDefinition: A personal promise to answer for a debt of the company. It undoes the limited liability at exactly that point.

managing_director_liability.shortDefinition: Whoever runs the company is personally liable in certain cases — unpaid social security contributions, or filing for insolvency too late.

bogus_self_employment.shortDefinition: When someone is formally treated as self-employed but actually works like an employee. Social security contributions then fall due retroactively.

articles_of_association.shortDefinition: The company's constitution: who holds which shares, how decisions are made, what happens when someone leaves. It overrides every spoken agreement.

shareholder_resolution.shortDefinition: The formal decision of the shareholders. Which topics need one and which majority counts is set out in the articles of association.

casting_vote.shortDefinition: A rule agreed in advance about whose vote decides a tie. It keeps a deadlock from paralysing the company.

blocking_minority.shortDefinition: A stake large enough to block important resolutions — for a GmbH usually from just over a quarter.

non_compete.shortDefinition: The agreement not to work for a competing business during the shareholding or afterwards. After someone leaves it is only valid within limits and often only against compensation.

severance_payment.shortDefinition: What someone receives for their shares when they leave. How it is calculated belongs in the contract — otherwise you argue about it precisely when things are already hard.

compulsory_redemption.shortDefinition: The rule that the company may take back shares against compensation — if someone becomes insolvent, say, or breaches essential duties.

transfer_restriction.shortDefinition: Shares may only be transferred with the consent of the other shareholders. That way nobody joins as a co-shareholder unasked.

succession_clause.shortDefinition: What happens to the shares when a shareholder dies: whether heirs step in, are paid out, or the shares are redeemed.

power_of_attorney.shortDefinition: Permission to act on someone else's behalf. Without it a lot comes to a standstill as soon as one person is out for a longer period.

account_authorization.shortDefinition: Who is allowed to dispose of the company's bank accounts. This is separate from power of attorney and from management, and usually has to be registered with the bank in its own right.

managing_director_contract.shortDefinition: The contract between the company and its management: duties, pay, holidays, termination. It is independent of who owns the shares.

prokura.shortDefinition: A far-reaching power of representation entered in the commercial register. Whoever holds it can conclude almost any business for the company.

advisory_board.shortDefinition: A body that advises and — depending on what was agreed — has a say in certain decisions. Unlike the shareholders' meeting it is voluntary.

nda.shortDefinition: The agreement not to pass certain information on. Common before talks with investors, partners or possible co-founders.

trademark.shortDefinition: The protected name or sign of an offering. Protection usually only arises with registration — not from using the name.

open_source_license.shortDefinition: The terms under which someone else's code may be used. Some require your own extensions to be published as well — which can become a problem in a later investment.

traction.shortDefinition: Demonstrable pull in the market: users, revenue, repeat purchases. What is meant is always the development over time, not a single figure.

unit_economics.shortDefinition: What a single unit — a customer, a subscription, an order — brings in and what it costs. It shows whether growth carries the business or consumes it.

arr_mrr.shortDefinition: Recurring revenue per year (ARR) or per month (MRR). The usual measure for subscription models.

churn.shortDefinition: The share of customers who leave within a period. High churn makes any growth expensive.

pitch_deck.shortDefinition: The short presentation a startup uses to introduce itself to investors: problem, solution, market, team, numbers, what it needs.
